docs.title: Cheesy Thumbprint Appetizers with Hot Pepper Jelly
docs.text: Savory cheddar thumbprint bites filled with sweet and spicy hot pepper jelly.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 cup shredded sharp cheddar cheese
  • 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard (optional)
  • 1/4 cup hot pepper jelly (or more to taste)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or lightly grease it.

  2. Make the dough: In a large bowl, combine softened butter, flour, shredded cheddar cheese, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Add Dijon mustard if using. Mix until a smooth, cohesive dough forms.

  3. Shape: Roll dough into 1-inch balls and place on prepared baking sheet about 1 inch apart.

  4. Create indentations: Use your thumb or the back of a spoon to press a small well into the center of each ball.

  5. Bake: Bake for 12–15 minutes, until edges are golden brown.

  6. Add jelly: Let cool for about 5 minutes. Spoon approximately 1/2 teaspoon hot pepper jelly into each indentation.

  7. Serve: Allow jelly to set slightly. Serve warm or at room temperature.

Prep Time: 10 minutes Cook Time: 15 minutes Total Time: 25 minutes Servings: 24 appetizers

docs.title: Classic Deviled Eggs
docs.text: Creamy, tangy deviled eggs perfect for gatherings and holidays.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 12 large eggs
  • 1/3 cup mayonnaise (or half mayo and half plain Greek yogurt)
  • 2 tablespoons pickle relish (or finely diced dill pickle)
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons Dijon mustard (or yellow mustard)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • Paprika, for garnish

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil.
  2. Once boiling, cover, remove from heat, and let sit for 10–12 minutes.
  3. Transfer eggs to an ice bath and cool completely.
  4. Peel eggs and slice in half lengthwise. Remove yolks and place them in a bowl.
  5. Mash yolks with mayonnaise, relish, mustard, salt, and pepper until smooth.
  6. Spoon or pipe filling back into egg whites.
  7. Sprinkle lightly with paprika before serving.

Store covered in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

docs.title: Greek yogurt
docs.text: title: Greek Beet Salad with Yogurt description: Roasted beets served over garlicky Greek yogurt with walnuts and fresh herbs. tags: - salad - greek - beet - appetizer

docs.title: Greek Beet Salad with Yogurt
docs.text: Source: Maria Koutsogiannis Date: 2023-10-18

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 4 large red beets
  • 1 cup Greek yogurt
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • Juice of half a lemon
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1/3 cup chopped walnuts
  • 2 tbsp fresh chopped mint
  • 2 tbsp fresh chopped dill

docs.title: 1. Roast the Beets
docs.text:
1. Wash the beets thoroughly and place them in foil.
  2. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
  3. Place the foil-wrapped beets on a baking sheet.
  4. Roast for 40–50 minutes, or until fork tender.
  5. Unwrap the beets and allow them to cool completely.
  6. Peel the skins off using your fingers or a vegetable peeler.

docs.title: 2. Slice the Beets
docs.text: Slice the peeled beets into wedges, about 6 wedges per beet, and set aside.

docs.title: 3. Prepare the Yogurt Base
docs.text:
In a small bowl, combine:

  • Greek yogurt
  • Olive oil
  • Minced garlic
  • Lemon juice
  • Salt

Mix until smooth.

docs.title: 4. Assemble the Salad
docs.text:
1. Spread the yogurt mixture onto a low bowl or serving platter.
  2. Arrange the beet wedges on top of the yogurt.
  3. Sprinkle with walnuts.
  4. Add chopped mint and dill.
  5. Finish with a pinch of salt if desired.

docs.title: Serving
docs.text:
Serve immediately.

Tags: #GreekFood #BeetSalad #GreekRecipes #PantzaroSalata

docs.title: Purple Radish Salad
docs.text: A quick and refreshing daikon radish salad with a tangy, slightly sweet sesame dressing. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 purple daikon radish, sliced into matchsticks
  • 1 carrot, sliced into matchsticks

docs.title: Dressing
docs.text:

docs.title: 1. Prep Vegetables
docs.text:
1. Wash and trim the radish and carrot.
  2. Slice both into matchsticks using a knife or julienne peeler.
  3. Transfer to a mixing bowl and add sliced green onions.

docs.title: 2. Make Dressing
docs.text:
In a small bowl, whisk together:

  • sesame oil
  • rice vinegar

  • lime juice

docs.title: 3. Assemble

1. Pour dressing over the vegetables.
  2. Toss until evenly coated.

docs.title: Cream Cheese Sausage Balls
docs.text: A rich, tender, cheesy sausage ball recipe using cream cheese for extra moisture and flavor.

docs.title: For the Sausage Balls
docs.text:
• 1 lb spicy pork sausage, ground and at room temperature
  • 1 (8 oz) block cream cheese, softened
  • 2 cups sharp cheddar cheese, shredded or pepper jack for heat
  • 1 1/4 cup Bisquick
  • 2 stalks scallions, finely chopped (optional)
  • 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder (optional)

docs.title: For the Dipping Sauce
docs.text:
• 2 tablespoons mayo
  • 2 tablespoons sweet chili sauce
  • OR use honey mustard (as referenced in the original recipe)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or lightly grease it.

  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the softened cream cheese and sausage. Use your hands or a mixer to blend until evenly mixed.

  3. Add shredded cheddar, Bisquick, scallions (if using), and garlic powder. Mix until everything is fully incorporated and a uniform dough forms.

  4. Roll the mixture into 1–1.5 inch balls and place them on the prepared baking sheet.

  5. Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until the sausage balls are golden brown and cooked through.

  6. While baking, prepare the dipping sauce by mixing mayo and sweet chili sauce until smooth.

  7. Serve warm with dipping sauce on the side.

docs.title: Baking & Sweets
docs.text:
From quick breakfast bakes to cozy cakes and bars, these are the recipes for slow mornings, shared tables, and keeping something good on the counter.

Zucchini Carrot Cake Honey Cream Cornbread Apple Cinnamon French Toast Poppables Apple Muffins with Crumb Topping Blueberry Butter Swim Biscuits Snickerdoodle Bars Sweet Potato Coffee Cake Carrot Cake Pancakes Morning Glory Muffins Easy Raspberry Jam Classic Waffles

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
The Cake * 2 cups carrots, shredded * 2 cups zucchini, shredded and drained * 4 eggs * 2 tbsp vanilla extract

The Frosting * 16 oz cream cheese * 8 tbsp butter

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray cake pans.
  2. Drain: Ensure zucchini is well drained.
  3. Mix: Combine wet ingredients.
  4. Bake: Bake for 35-45 minutes.

Chef's Tip

Make sure to really squeeze the water out of the zucchini or the cake will be soggy!

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup yellow cornmeal
  • 1/4 cup white sugar
  • 1 tablespoon baking powder
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 2 large eggs, lightly beaten
  • 1/4 cup vegetable oil
  • 1/4 cup honey

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Lightly grease a 9x9-inch baking pan.

  2. Mix dry ingredients: In a large bowl, stir together the flour, cornmeal, sugar, and baking powder. Form a well in the center.

  3. Add wet ingredients: Add the heavy cream, eggs, vegetable oil, and honey. Stir until well combined.

  4. Bake: Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan. Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.

  5. Cool and serve: Let cool slightly before slicing. Serve warm, optionally topped with butter and additional honey.

docs.title: Apple Cinnamon French Toast Poppables
docs.text: Freezer-friendly breakfast bites and a smart way to use up leftover bread (including crusts).

docs.title: Custard Base
docs.text:
• 8 eggs
  • 2 cups milk
  • 3/4 cup brown sugar
  • 1 tbsp cinnamon
  • Splash of vanilla
  • Dried bread cubes (enough to soak up the custard)
  • 2 cups peeled and finely chopped apples

docs.title: Crumb Topping
docs.text:
• 3/4 cup brown sugar
  • 3/4 cup flour
  • 1 tsp cinnamon
  • 2–3 tbsp melted butter or margarine (enough to make a “wet sand” texture)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Cut leftover bread (or crusts) into cubes and let them dry out overnight.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, brown sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla.
  3. Fold in the dried bread cubes and chopped apples. Add just enough bread so the liquid is absorbed.
  4. Divide mixture into 24 greased muffin tins (or use silicone pans).
  5. Mix the crumb topping ingredients and sprinkle over the top.
  6. Bake at 350°F for 25 minutes.
  7. Cool completely before freezing. Reheat in the microwave or toaster oven.

docs.title: Apple Muffins with Crumb Topping & Maple Syrup Icing
Muffins
docs.text:
• 1 and 3/4 cups all-purpose flour or whole wheat OR replace 3/4 cup with protein pancake mix
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup softened unsalted butter or replace 1/4 cup of the butter with applesauce for a healthier version
  • 1/2 cup packed light or dark brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 1/2 cup Greek yogurt (unsweetened or vanilla), at room temperature
  • 2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract
  • 1/4 cup milk (any kind), at room temperature
  • 1 and 1/2 cups peeled & chopped apples

docs.title: Crumb Topping
docs.text:
• 1/4 cup dark brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 cup melted unsalted butter
  • 2/3 cup all-purpose flour or whole wheat flour

docs.title: Maple Syrup Icing
docs.text:
• 1 cup confectioners’ sugar
  • 3 tablespoons half and half
  • 1 teaspoon maple syrup

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F. Spray a muffin pan with nonstick spray or line with cupcake liners. Recipe makes 12–14 muffins.

  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt. Set aside.

  3. In a separate bowl, beat the butter and both sugars on high speed until smooth and creamy (about 2 minutes). Add the eggs, yogurt, and vanilla. Beat on medium speed for 1 minute, then increase to high speed until the mixture is combined and mostly creamy. It’s ok if it looks slightly curdled. Scrape down the bowl as needed.

  4. With the mixer on low speed, add the dry ingredients and milk into the wet mixture. Mix until no flour pockets remain. Fold in the chopped apples.

  5. Make the crumb topping: In a medium bowl, mix the brown sugar, granulated sugar, and cinnamon. Stir in the melted butter, then gently mix in the flour with a fork. Keep the mixture as large crumbles and do not over-mix (overmixing turns it into a paste).

  6. Spoon the batter evenly into muffin cups, filling each to the top. Add crumb topping to each and gently press so it sticks.

  7. Bake for 5 minutes at 425°F, then (without opening the oven) reduce temperature to 350°F. Bake an additional 15–18 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Total bake time: 20–23 minutes.

  8. Allow muffins to cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.

  9. Make the icing: Whisk together all icing ingredients. Drizzle over warm or cooled muffins.

  10. Store iced or plain muffins at room temperature for 2–3 days, or in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

docs.title: Blueberry Butter Swim Biscuits
docs.text: Soft, buttery buttermilk biscuits baked in a butter bath and topped with a sweet glaze.

docs.title: Butter Bath
docs.text: • 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, melted

docs.title: Biscuit Dough
docs.text:
• 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar
  • 1 tablespoon baking powder (aluminum-free preferred)
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 3/4 cups buttermilk (add a splash more if dough seems dry)
  • 1 1/2 cups fresh or frozen blueberries

docs.title: Glaze (optional but recommended)
docs.text:
• 1 cup powdered sugar
  • 2–3 tablespoons milk

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat & prep: Preheat oven to 450°F (232°C). Lightly grease a 9x9-inch (or 8x8-inch) baking dish.

  2. Butter bath: Pour melted butter into the baking dish, swirling to coat the bottom evenly.

  3. Mix dry ingredients: In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.

  4. Add buttermilk: Stir in buttermilk until a sticky dough forms. Add a splash more if needed.

  5. Fold in blueberries: Gently mix in blueberries to avoid bursting.

  6. Bake: Spoon the dough over the melted butter in the dish and spread gently. Lightly score into 9 squares with a knife. Bake on the middle rack for 25–30 minutes, until golden and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.

  7. Glaze & serve: While baking, whisk powdered sugar and milk to desired drizzling consistency. Drizzle over warm biscuits. Let cool slightly, slice, and serve.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 3/4 cup unsalted butter, fully melted
  • 3/4 cup packed brown sugar
  • 1 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 2 teaspoons pure vanilla extract
  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon cream of tartar
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt

docs.title: Topping
docs.text:
• 1/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 teaspoons cinnamon

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. In a large bowl, combine melted butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar. Mix well.
  3. Add eggs and vanilla extract. Mix until fully incorporated.
  4. In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, cream of tartar, and salt.
  5. Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients and mix until combined.
  6. Line a 9x9-inch baking dish with parchment paper.
  7. Evenly spread batter into prepared baking dish.
  8. In a small bowl, mix together granulated sugar and cinnamon for the topping.
  9. Sprinkle topping evenly over the batter.
  10. Bake for 27 minutes, or until set and lightly golden.
  11. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

docs.title: Yield
docs.text: • Makes 8 large bars

docs.title: Sweet Potato Coffee Cake
docs.text: Moist, warmly spiced coffee cake made with mashed sweet potatoes and topped with a cinnamon crumb.

docs.title: Cake Batter
docs.text:
• 3/4 cup cane sugar
  • 1/2 cup melted butter
  • 2 eggs
  • 2 tablespoons maple syrup
  • 2 cups mashed sweet potatoes (about 2 large; boiled, peeled, and mashed)
  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 2 teaspoons pumpkin spice
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

docs.title: Cinnamon Layer
docs.text:
• 2 tablespoons coconut sugar or brown sugar
  • 1 teaspoon cinnamon

docs.title: Crumb Topping
docs.text:
• 5 tablespoons flour
  • 1/4 cup coconut sugar or brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup cane sugar
  • 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
  • 1/4 cup softened butter

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 9x9-inch baking dish.

  2. In a large bowl, combine cane sugar, melted butter, eggs, maple syrup, and mashed sweet potatoes. Mix with a hand mixer for about 1 minute. (Some small sweet potato clumps are fine.)

  3. Add flour, baking powder, pumpkin spice, and salt. Stir until a thick batter forms.

  4. Pour half of the batter into the prepared pan. Sprinkle evenly with coconut or brown sugar and cinnamon. Pour the remaining batter over the top.

  5. In a small bowl, mix flour, sugars, cinnamon, and softened butter until crumbly. Sprinkle over the batter.

  6. Bake for 45 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

  7. Cool on a wire rack for about 20 minutes before slicing and serving.

docs.title: Carrot Cake Pancakes
docs.text: These carrot cake pancakes are rich, warmly spiced, and topped with a maple cream cheese drizzle. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

docs.title: Pancakes
docs.text:
• 2 cups finely grated carrots (about 6 large or 8 small)
  • 1 cup (125 g) whole wheat pastry flour (or whole wheat or all-purpose flour)
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1/2 teaspoon fine salt
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 tablespoons coconut sugar or brown sugar
  • 1 cup buttermilk
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Avocado oil or butter, for cooking

docs.title: Maple Cream Cheese Topping
docs.text:
• 4 oz cream cheese, softened
  • 2 tablespoons maple syrup (plus more for serving)
  • 2 tablespoons milk (adjust for consistency)
  • 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Dash of cinnamon
  • Optional: chopped toasted walnuts or pecans

docs.title: 1. Prepare Ingredients
docs.text:
1. Soften cream cheese by letting it sit at room temperature.
  2. Place grated carrots in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with a damp paper towel, and microwave for 2 minutes.
  3. Let carrots cool.
  4. Optional: preheat oven to 200°F to keep pancakes warm.

docs.title: 2. Mix Dry Ingredients
docs.text:
In a large bowl, whisk together:

  • flour
  • baking powder
  • baking soda
  • salt
  • cinnamon
  • nutmeg
  • ginger

docs.title: 3. Mix Wet Ingredients
docs.text:
In a separate bowl:

  1. Whisk egg and sugar.
  2. Add buttermilk and vanilla.
  3. Stir in cooled carrots.

docs.title: 4. Combine Batter
docs.text:
1. Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients.
  2. Stir until just combined.
  3. Let batter rest for 5 minutes.

docs.title: 5. Make Topping
docs.text:
1. Whisk cream cheese until smooth.
  2. Add maple syrup, milk, vanilla, and cinnamon.
  3. Adjust sweetness and consistency as desired.

docs.title: 6. Cook Pancakes
docs.text:
1. Heat a skillet or griddle over medium-low heat (or 350°F).
  2. Lightly grease the surface.
  3. Scoop 1/4 cup batter per pancake.
  4. Cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles form and edges set.
  5. Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more until golden.
  6. Repeat with remaining batter.

docs.title: 7. Serve
docs.text:
• Top pancakes with maple cream cheese.
  • Add chopped nuts if desired.
  • Serve with additional maple syrup.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• Refrigerate leftovers up to 4 days
  • Freeze up to 6 months

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• To make buttermilk: mix 1 cup milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar; let sit 5 minutes.
  • For dairy-free: use plant-based milk and dairy-free cream cheese.
  • Avoid overmixing batter to keep pancakes fluffy.

docs.title: Morning Glory Muffins
docs.text: These cinnamon-spiced muffins are packed with whole wheat flour, apples, carrots, raisins, honey, and warm spices. They taste like a combination of apple cake, spice cake, and carrot cake—perfect for breakfast. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 cups (260 g) whole wheat flour
  • 2 teaspoons baking soda
  • 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/3 cup (35 g) ground flaxseed (optional)

docs.title: Wet Ingredients
docs.text:
• 3 large eggs, room temperature
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) packed brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup (85 g) honey
  • 1/3 cup (80 ml) vegetable oil, canola oil, or melted coconut oil
  • 1/3 cup (80 g) unsweetened applesauce
  • 1 teaspoon orange zest (optional)
  • 1/3 cup (80 ml) orange juice or pineapple juice
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

docs.title: Mix-ins
docs.text:
• 2 cups (260 g) shredded carrots (about 4 large)
  • 1 cup (140 g) shredded apple (about 1 large)
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) raisins
  • 1/2 cup (64 g) chopped pecans

docs.title: 1. Preheat Oven
docs.text:
Preheat oven to 425°F (218°C).

Grease a 12-count muffin pan or line with muffin liners. This recipe makes 14–16 muffins, so prepare a second pan or bake in batches.

docs.title: 2. Mix Dry Ingredients
docs.text:
In a large bowl whisk together:

  • whole wheat flour
  • baking soda
  • cinnamon
  • ginger
  • salt
  • flaxseed (optional)

docs.title: 3. Mix Wet Ingredients
docs.text:
In a separate bowl whisk together:

  • eggs
  • brown sugar
  • honey
  • oil
  • applesauce
  • orange zest
  • orange juice
  • vanilla extract

Mix until fully combined.

docs.title: 4. Combine Batter
docs.text:
1. Stir carrots and shredded apple into the wet mixture.
  2. Pour wet ingredients into the dry ingredients.
  3. Stir a few times.
  4. Add raisins and pecans.
  5. Fold until just combined and no dry flour remains.

docs.title: 5. Fill Muffin Pan
docs.text: Spoon batter into muffin liners, filling all the way to the top.

docs.title: 6. Bake
docs.text:
1. Bake 5 minutes at 425°F (218°C).
  2. Without removing muffins, reduce oven temperature to 350°F (177°C).
  3. Bake an additional 18 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

Total baking time: 23–24 minutes.

docs.title: 7. Cool
docs.text: Allow muffins to cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• Store covered at room temperature for 2 days
  • Refrigerate for up to 1 week

docs.title: Freezing
docs.text: Muffins freeze well for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and warm if desired.

docs.title: Simple Morning Glory Muffins
docs.text: Moist, warmly spiced muffins packed with carrots, apple, raisins, and pecans.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 cups (260g) whole wheat flour (measured correctly)
  • 2 teaspoons baking soda
  • 2 teaspoons ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/3 cup (35g) ground flax (optional)
  • 1/2 cup (64g) unsalted chopped pecans
  • 3 large eggs
  • 1/2 cup (100g) packed light or dark brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup (85g) honey
  • Substitute: agave or maple syrup, or use 1/4 cup additional brown sugar
  • 1/3 cup (80ml) vegetable oil, canola oil, or melted coconut oil
  • 1/3 cup (60g) smooth applesauce
  • Substitute: 1/3 cup additional oil or mashed banana (may be slightly drier)
  • 1 teaspoon orange zest
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) orange juice or pineapple juice
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup (75g) raisins, soaked in warm water for 10 minutes and drained
  • Optional: use golden raisins, dried cranberries, or omit
  • 2 cups (260g) shredded carrots (about 4 large)
  • 1 cup (140g) shredded or grated apple (about 1 apple; any variety works, e.g., Granny Smith)

docs.title: Directions
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F (218°C). Spray a 12-count muffin pan with nonstick spray or line with cupcake liners. This recipe makes about 16 muffins, so prepare a second pan if needed.

  2. Mix dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, salt, flax (if using), and pecans. Set aside.

  3. Mix wet ingredients: In a medium bowl, whisk together eggs, brown sugar, honey, oil, applesauce, orange zest, orange juice, and vanilla until combined.

  4. Combine: Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir gently a few times, then fold in raisins, shredded carrots, and apple. Mix just until combined—do not overmix.

  5. Fill pans: Spoon batter into liners, filling each all the way to the top.

  6. Bake:

  7. Bake for 5 minutes at 425°F (218°C).
  8. Without removing muffins, reduce oven temperature to 350°F (177°C).

  9. Bake for an additional 18 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

  10. Cool: Allow muffins to cool in the pan for several minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The initial high temperature helps create tall muffin tops.
  • Store at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate up to 1 week.
  • Muffins freeze well for up to 3 months.

docs.title: Easy Raspberry Jam (No Pectin)
docs.text: A simple 3-ingredient raspberry jam that is sweet, tangy, and beginner-friendly. This recipe uses no added pectin and can be stored in the fridge, freezer, or canned for long-term storage. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
• 6 glass jars (8 oz / 250 ml)
  • Large heavy-bottom saucepan
  • Silicone spatula or wooden spoon
  • Potato masher or fork
  • Canning funnel
  • Food thermometer
  • Sieve or jelly bag (optional)
  • Bubble remover (optional)
  • Magnetic lid wand (optional)
  • Canning pot
  • Canning tongs

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2.2 lb raspberries (about 8 cups)
  • 4 cups white sugar (28 oz)
  • 1/4 cup lemon juice (fresh or bottled)

docs.title: 1. Prepare the Berries and Jars
docs.text:
1. Sterilize jars, lids, and bands by washing in hot soapy water or running through a dishwasher.
  2. Allow jars to dry and keep them warm until ready to use.
  3. Place 1–2 small plates in the freezer for the gel test.
  4. If canning, prepare a water bath canner with a rack and enough water to cover jars by 1 inch.
  5. Wash raspberries thoroughly and remove stems or spoiled berries.

docs.title: 2. Simmer the Jam
docs.text:
1. Add raspberries and sugar to a large stainless-steel saucepan.
  2. Gently crush berries with a potato masher, leaving some whole if desired.
  3. Add lemon juice and stir.
  4. Bring mixture to a full rolling boil, stirring constantly so sugar dissolves.
  5. Skim foam from the surface as it forms.
  6. Simmer 15–20 minutes, until the jam thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.

docs.title: 3. Gel Test
docs.text:
1. Remove pan from heat.
  2. Place 1 teaspoon jam on a frozen plate.
  3. Return plate to freezer for 1–2 minutes.
  4. Push jam with your finger — it should wrinkle if set.

Alternative: Use a thermometer. Jam sets at 220°F (104°C).

If not set, cook a few minutes longer and test again.

docs.title: 4. Fill the Jars
docs.text:
1. Place warm sterilized jars on a towel or wooden board.
  2. Ladle hot jam into jars leaving ¼ inch headspace.
  3. Tap jars gently or run a knife inside to remove air bubbles.
  4. Wipe jar rims clean.
  5. Add lids and tighten bands fingertip tight.

At this point the jam can be:

  • used immediately
  • refrigerated for short-term storage
  • frozen for up to 6 months
  • water bath canned for long storage

docs.title: 5. Water Bath Canning (Optional)
docs.text:
1. Place filled jars in the canner so they are covered with at least 1 inch of water.
  2. Bring to a boil and process for 10 minutes (adjust for altitude).
  3. Turn off heat and let jars sit 5 minutes.
  4. Remove jars with tongs and cool on a towel 24 hours undisturbed.
  5. Check seals (lid center should not pop).

Store sealed jars in a cool dark pantry for up to 12–18 months.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Use ripe but not overripe raspberries for best flavor and natural pectin.
  • Always use non-reactive cookware (stainless steel, enamel, glass).
  • If jam is too runny, return it to the pan and cook longer.
  • For seedless jam, push finished jam through a fine mesh sieve.

docs.title: Mexican Picadillo
docs.text:
Mexican Picadillo

This dinner is always on rotation at our house because it is so flavorful but comes together really easily. It is definitely a household favorite.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 green bell pepper
  • 1 onion
  • 3–4 small or 2 large potatoes
  • 1 lb ground beef
  • Chili powder, to taste
  • Cumin, to taste
  • Coriander, to taste
  • Paprika, to taste
  • Oregano, to taste
  • Salt and pepper, to taste
  • Garlic, minced (to taste)
  • 1 (15 oz) can beef broth
  • 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce
  • 1 bay leaf
  • Green olives, sliced (optional)
  • Cooked white rice, for serving
  • Flour tortillas, for serving
  • Fresh cilantro, for serving

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Prep all vegetables (dice bell pepper, onion, and potatoes; mince garlic).
  2. In a large pan, brown the ground beef over medium heat. Drain excess grease if necessary.
  3. Add the bell pepper, onion, potatoes, garlic, and all seasonings (chili powder, cumin, coriander, paprika, oregano, salt, and pepper). Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables start to soften.
  4. Stir in the beef broth and tomato sauce.
  5. Bring the mixture to a simmer and add the bay leaf.
  6. Cover and cook for 10 minutes.
  7. Remove the lid and simmer for an additional 10 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender and the mixture has slightly thickened.
  8. Stir in green olives, if using.
  9. Serve the picadillo over white rice with a warm flour tortilla and fresh cilantro.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 2 pounds ground chuck
  • 1/2 cup crushed saltine crackers or Panko breadcrumbs
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce
  • 2 tablespoons milk
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Lightly grease a loaf pan or line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

  2. Prepare the binder: In a large bowl, combine the crushed saltine crackers and milk. Let them sit for 2–3 minutes to soften.

  3. Mix the meatloaf: Add the ground chuck, egg, Worcestershire sauce, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper to the bowl. Using clean hands or a spoon, gently mix until the ingredients are just combined. Do not overmix, or the meatloaf may become dense.

  4. Shape the loaf: Transfer the mixture to the prepared pan or baking sheet. Shape it into a tight, even loaf about 9 inches long.

  5. (Optional but recommended) Add a topping: Spread 1/2 cup ketchup or a mix of ketchup + BBQ sauce over the top. For a more savory version, leave plain.

  6. Bake: Place in the oven and bake for 55–65 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 160°F.

  7. Rest the meatloaf: Remove from the oven and let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing. This helps the juices redistribute and keeps the slices from falling apart.

docs.title: Lemongrass and Ginger Pork Patties
docs.text: Course: Main Cuisine: Dairy free, gluten free, nut free, sugar free Prep Time: 20 minutes Cook Time: 20 minutes Total Time: 40 minutes Servings: 5 Calories: 323 kcal (per serving)

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 500 g (18 oz) lean pork mince
  • 1 egg
  • 1.5 tablespoons minced or finely chopped lemongrass
  • 1 tablespoon grated ginger fresh or jarred
  • 2 cloves garlic, crushed or 2 teaspoons jarred minced garlic
  • 1 tablespoon soy sauce use gluten-free soy sauce or tamari if needed
  • 2 teaspoons honey or maple syrup
  • 3 spring onions, finely sliced
  • 1/2 cup quick oats or breadcrumbs use gluten-free oats/breadcrumbs if needed
  • Pinch of black pepper
  • Extra virgin olive oil, for cooking

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a large baking tray with baking paper. Set aside.

  2. Prepare aromatics: peel and grate the ginger, crush the garlic, and finely slice the spring onions.

  3. In a large bowl, combine everything except the olive oil: pork mince, egg, oats/breadcrumbs, lemongrass, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, honey, spring onions, and pepper. Mix well and shape into 14–16 small patties (like large, slightly flattened meatballs).

  4. Heat a large frying pan over high heat and add 1 tablespoon olive oil. Cook patties for 2 minutes per side, just until browned. Transfer browned patties to the lined baking tray as you go.

  5. Once all patties are browned, place the baking tray in the oven and bake for 10–12 minutes, or until cooked through.

  6. Serve patties with rice or noodles and a crunchy fresh salad. Leftovers will keep refrigerated for up to 3 days.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Nutrition values use regular pork mince; lean mince will alter the numbers.
  • You can substitute chicken mince or turkey mince for pork.
  • Patties can be frozen raw or cooked. Place baking paper between patties to prevent sticking.
  • Dressing suggestion: Mix sweet chili sauce, a splash of soy sauce, and fresh lime juice. Rice vinegar can be used instead of lime. Add crushed peanuts or toasted cashews for extra crunch and flavor.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 1/2 oz. plain whole-milk yogurt
  • 2 tsp. kosher salt, plus more
  • 1 1/2 tsp. ground turmeric
  • 1 tsp. finely grated lime zest or ground sumac
  • 1 tsp. ground cinnamon
  • 1 tsp. ground cumin
  • 1/4 tsp. freshly ground black pepper, plus more
  • 1/4 tsp. ground cloves
  • 1/4 tsp. ground coriander
  • 1/8 tsp. cayenne pepper
  • 4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 1 1/2 lb.)
  • 4 whole chicken drumsticks (about 1 1/2 lb.)
  • 2 bone-in, skin-on chicken breasts (about 2 lb.), halved crosswise
  • 1 pint grape tomatoes
  • 1 lemon, quartered
  • Neutral oil, for brushing and grill
  • Steamed jasmine rice (optional)
  • Fresh cilantro, parsley, and mint leaves, for serving

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Prepare the marinade: In a large bowl, mix yogurt, salt, turmeric, lime zest (or sumac), cinnamon, cumin, black pepper, cloves, coriander, and cayenne.

  2. Marinate the chicken: Add chicken pieces and turn to coat thoroughly. Transfer chicken and marinade to a resealable plastic bag. Seal and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or up to 24 hours.

  3. Bring to room temperature: Let chicken sit at room temperature for 30 minutes before grilling. Thread tomatoes and lemon wedges onto skewers. Brush with oil and season with salt and pepper.

  4. Prepare the grill: Preheat grill to medium-high heat (about 5 minutes). Clean and oil grates. Brush excess marinade off chicken; discard marinade.

  5. Grill the chicken: Place chicken skin side down and grill until skin is golden brown, about 15 minutes. Turn and continue grilling until skin is charred and chicken is cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 160°F, about 10 minutes more.

  6. Rest: Transfer chicken to a plate and tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.

  7. Grill skewers: Grill tomato and lemon skewers, turning occasionally, until charred in spots, 5–6 minutes. Remove from skewers.

  8. Serve: Serve chicken and tomatoes with rice (if using). Squeeze grilled lemon wedges over the top. Garnish with cilantro, parsley, and mint.

docs.title: The Coziest Dutch Oven Chicken Dinner
docs.text: Creamy, cozy Dutch oven chicken with baby potatoes and green beans. Perfect served over egg noodles.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon paprika
  • 1 teaspoon fine sea salt
  • 1 teaspoon onion powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
  • 2 full-size boneless skinless chicken breasts
  • 1/4 cup butter
  • 1 medium yellow onion, diced (about 1 cup)
  • 3 medium cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 1/2 teaspoons dried thyme leaves
  • 1 1/2 cups chicken broth (or more if preferred)
  • 1 1/2 pounds baby potatoes, halved
  • Handful of green beans
  • 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup whole milk or half-and-half cream

docs.title: 1. Season the Chicken
docs.text:
1. In a bowl, combine:
  2. Olive oil
  3. Paprika
  4. Salt
  5. Onion powder

  6. Black pepper

  7. Slice the chicken breasts horizontally so you have 4 thinner pieces.

  8. Add chicken to the bowl and toss until evenly coated.

docs.title: 2. Sear the Chicken
docs.text:
1. Heat a Dutch oven over medium heat for about 4 minutes.
  2. Add the seasoned chicken and cook for about 2 minutes per side.
  3. Transfer chicken to a plate and set aside.

docs.title: 3. Build the Base
docs.text:
1. Add butter to the Dutch oven.
  2. Once melted, add diced onion and sauté for about 4 minutes.
  3. Stir in garlic and thyme; cook until fragrant.

docs.title: 4. Make the Sauce
docs.text:
1. Sprinkle flour over the onion mixture and stir thoroughly.
  2. Cook for 2 minutes.
  3. Slowly whisk in:
  4. Chicken broth

  5. Milk or half-and-half

  6. Whisk until smooth and thickened.

docs.title: 5. Add Vegetables
docs.text:
1. Add baby potatoes and green beans.
  2. Increase heat and bring to a boil.
  3. Boil for about 4 minutes.
  4. Remove from heat.

docs.title: 6. Bake
docs.text:
1. Add the chicken back to the pot.
  2. Cover with the lid.
  3. Bake in a preheated 400°F oven for 15–17 minutes, or until:
  4. Potatoes are fork-tender
  5. Chicken is fully cooked

docs.title: Serving
docs.text: Serve warm over egg noodles.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Add extra broth if you prefer a thinner sauce.
  • Fresh thyme may be substituted for dried (use ~1 tablespoon).
  • Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C).

Prep Time: ~10 minutes Cook Time: ~25–30 minutes Total Time: ~40 minutes Servings: 4

docs.title: Creamy Garlic Butter Rigatoni with Ground Beef and Parmesan
docs.text: Rich, creamy pasta with seasoned ground beef, garlic butter sauce, and Parmesan.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text: • 8 ounces rigatoni (or preferred pasta)

docs.title: Beef & Sauce
docs.text:
• 1 lb ground beef
  • 1 teaspoon dried Italian seasoning
  • 1 1/2 cups heavy cream (adjust for desired creaminess)
  • 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
  • 1 teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons butter
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • 2 1/2 cups beef broth (adjust as needed for liquid)

docs.title: Garnish
docs.text: • Fresh chopped parsley (optional)

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. In a large pot over medium heat, melt the butter.

  2. Add ground beef and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and fully cooked.

  3. Stir in minced garlic and chopped onion. Cook for 2–3 minutes until softened and fragrant.

  4. Sprinkle in Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.

  5. Pour in beef broth and heavy cream. Stir to combine and bring to a gentle simmer.

  6. Add rigatoni, ensuring it is fully submerged in the liquid. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 15–20 minutes, until pasta is tender and sauce thickens. Add more broth if needed.

  7. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and cook for another 1–2 minutes until sauce becomes creamy.

  8. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired. Serve warm.

Total Time: 30–35 minutes Calories: ~450 per serving

docs.title: Creamy Italian Sausage and Gnocchi Soup
docs.text: Rich, creamy, and hearty soup packed with Italian sausage, vegetables, gnocchi, spinach, and Parmesan.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 lb Italian sausage
  • 1 onion, diced
  • 2 carrots, diced
  • 2 ribs celery, diced
  • 6–7 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1/4 cup sun-dried tomatoes
  • 1 tsp herbs de Provence (or Italian seasoning)
  • 2 cups chicken broth
  • 1 lb gnocchi
  • 2 cups fresh chopped baby spinach
  • 2 cups heavy cream
  • 3 oz freshly grated Parmesan cheese
  • Salt and pepper, to taste

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. In a large pot, brown the Italian sausage with diced onion, carrots, and celery until the meat is fully cooked and vegetables are softened.

  2. Add minced garlic and sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for about 1 minute until fragrant.

  3. Stir in herbs de Provence (or Italian seasoning), chicken broth, and gnocchi. Bring to a boil and cook for 2–3 minutes.

  4. Add fresh spinach and allow it to wilt.

  5. Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan.

  6. Simmer on low for about 30 minutes, until the soup thickens.

  7. Season to taste with salt and pepper if needed. Serve warm.

docs.title: Grilled Chicken Alfredo Pasta
docs.text: Source: Secrets of Liya Date: 2023-06-02

docs.title: For the Chicken Marinade
docs.text:
• 3 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
  • 1 tbsp smoked paprika
  • 1/2 tbsp black pepper
  • 1/2 tbsp salt
  • 1/2 tbsp garlic powder
  • 1/2 tbsp dried parsley
  • A pinch of rosemary

docs.title: Pasta
docs.text: • Penne pasta (boiled according to package instructions)

docs.title: Alfredo Sauce
docs.text:
• 4 tbsp butter
  • 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
  • 8 oz milk
  • 1/2 cup heavy cream
  • 3 tbsp cream cheese
  • 1/3 cup mozzarella cheese
  • 1/3 cup parmesan cheese
  • 1 tbsp red chili flakes
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • 1 tbsp dried parsley
  • 1 tbsp oregano

docs.title: 1. Prepare and Grill the Chicken
docs.text:
1. Season the chicken breasts with smoked paprika, black pepper, salt, garlic powder, dried parsley, and rosemary.
  2. Grill for 6–8 minutes per side, or until fully cooked.
  3. Remove from heat and let rest for a few minutes.
  4. Slice into thin strips.

docs.title: 2. Make the Alfredo Sauce
docs.text:
1. In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat.
  2. Add the flour and whisk until smooth, keeping the heat low.
  3. Slowly add the milk while stirring continuously.
  4. Add the cream cheese and heavy cream. Stir until smooth and creamy.
  5. Add mozzarella and parmesan cheese.
  6. Stir in red chili flakes, parsley, oregano, salt, and pepper to taste.
  7. Continue stirring until the sauce thickens and becomes smooth.

docs.title: 3. Assemble
docs.text:
1. Add the cooked penne pasta to the skillet and toss until fully coated in the Alfredo sauce.
  2. Top with sliced grilled chicken.
  3. Garnish with additional parsley if desired.

docs.title: Serve
docs.text: Serve warm and enjoy.

docs.title: Ground Beef and Cabbage Gratin
docs.text: Prep Time: 10 minutes Cook Time: 50 minutes Yield: 4 servings

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 lb ground beef
  • 1 medium white cabbage, chopped
  • 1 yellow onion, chopped
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon paprika
  • Pinch of cayenne

docs.title: For the Topping
docs.text:
• 3 eggs
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 1 cup grated parmesan cheese

docs.title: Instructions
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).

  2. In a large oven-safe skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the ground beef and cook for 8–10 minutes, breaking it apart as it browns.

  3. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 3–4 minutes until soft and translucent.

  4. Stir in the chopped cabbage, salt, black pepper, paprika, and cayenne. Cook for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage softens and begins to brown slightly.

  5. In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, heavy cream, and grated parmesan cheese.

  6. Pour the egg and cream mixture evenly over the beef and cabbage mixture in the skillet, ensuring the surface is covered.

  7. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for 30–35 minutes, or until the top is golden and bubbly and the center is set.

  8. Let cool for 5–10 minutes before serving directly from the skillet.

docs.title: Roasted Beet Borscht
docs.text: A traditional beet soup with roasted beets for deeper flavor.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 cup celery, diced
  • 1 cup onions, diced
  • 1 cup cabbage, chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, grated or pressed
  • 1 tablespoon butter (for sautéing vegetables)
  • 8 cups water or beef/chicken broth
  • 1 can diced tomatoes (28 oz or 1 quart home-canned)
  • 2 large beets or 3 medium beets
  • 1 large carrot or 2 medium, grated
  • 1 medium potato, diced
  • 1/2 cup fresh dill weed
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste
  • 1 bay leaf (optional)
  • Oil (for roasting beets)

docs.title: Roast the Beets
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
  2. Lightly coat beets with oil.
  3. Wrap beets in aluminum foil and place on a baking sheet.
  4. Roast for 45–60 minutes, until tender.
  5. Let cool for 10 minutes, then peel.
  6. Slice into 1/4-inch slices or dice as desired.

docs.title: Make the Soup
docs.text:
1. In a large pot, sauté onions, celery, and cabbage in butter until soft and translucent.
  2. Add garlic and cook briefly.
  3. Add diced tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil.
  4. Add roasted beets, grated carrots, diced potato, and bay leaf.
  5. Reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 15–20 minutes.
  6. Stir in fresh dill, salt, and pepper.
  7. Remove bay leaf before serving.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• Cool completely before storing.
  • Freeze up to 3 months in airtight containers.
  • Thaw overnight and reheat gently on stovetop.

docs.title: Easy Homemade Chili

docs.title: Sweet 'n Sticky Baked Chicken Drumsticks
docs.text: Sweet, savory, and caramelized baked chicken drumsticks finished with a thick sticky glaze. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1/2 cup balsamic vinegar
  • 1/2 cup honey
  • 1/2 cup packed light brown sugar
  • 1/4 cup low-sodium soy sauce
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 12 chicken drumsticks
  • 2 tablespoons sesame seeds
  • 1/4 cup chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley

docs.title: 1. Marinate the Chicken
docs.text:
1. In a large resealable bag, combine:
  2. balsamic vinegar
  3. honey
  4. brown sugar
  5. soy sauce

  6. minced garlic

  7. Add the chicken drumsticks and seal the bag.

  8. Marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours.

docs.title: 2. Bake the Chicken
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 450°F (232°C).
  2. Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil.
  3. Place a cooling rack on top of the baking sheet.
  4. Remove chicken from the marinade, reserving the marinade.
  5. Arrange drumsticks on the rack.
  6. Bake for about 30 minutes, until skin is caramelized and dark in spots.

docs.title: 3. Make the Sticky Glaze
docs.text:
1. Pour the reserved marinade into a small saucepan.
  2. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat.
  3. Simmer about 15 minutes, until thickened.

docs.title: 4. Finish the Chicken
docs.text:
1. Brush the thickened glaze over the baked chicken.
  2. Return to the oven for 10 more minutes.

docs.title: 5. Serve
docs.text:
1. Transfer chicken to a serving platter.
  2. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and chopped parsley.
  3. Serve warm.

Yield: 12 drumsticks

docs.title: Parmesan Crusted Crushed Turnips
docs.text: A delicious, crispy, low-carb alternative to crushed potatoes with a golden Parmesan crust. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
• Large pot or stockpot
  • Potato masher
  • Pastry brush
  • Parchment paper
  • Rimmed baking sheet

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 12 small to medium turnips, peeled
  • Salt
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 1 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (or as needed)
  • Fresh chives, chopped (for garnish)

docs.title: 1. Cook the Turnips
docs.text:
1. Place peeled turnips in a pot and cover with salted water.
  2. Bring to a boil and cook for 20–30 minutes, until easily pierced with a knife.
  3. Drain and let cool slightly.

docs.title: 2. Prep for Baking
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. Place turnips on a clean kitchen towel or paper towels.
  3. Gently press each turnip down to about 1/2-inch thickness.
  4. Let drain for 15 minutes, then flip and allow the other side to dry.

docs.title: 3. Season
docs.text:
1. In a small bowl, combine:
  2. olive oil
  3. minced garlic
  4. salt
  5. black pepper

docs.title: 4. Assemble
docs.text:
1. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or foil.
  2. Place flattened turnips on the sheet.
  3. Brush each with the oil and garlic mixture.
  4. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese over each, pressing lightly.
  5. Carefully flip each turnip and repeat seasoning and cheese on the other side.

docs.title: 5. Bake
docs.text:
1. Bake for 20–25 minutes.
  2. Flip each turnip.
  3. Bake an additional 15 minutes, until golden and crisp.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text: Garnish with chopped fresh chives and serve warm.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Substitute Parmesan with Asiago, Romano, or Manchego if desired.
  • Flip quickly to keep the cheese coating intact.
  • Avoid overcooking to maintain texture.

docs.title: Instant Pot Option
docs.text:
1. Add rack and 1 1/2 cups water (6-qt) or 2 cups (8-qt).
  2. Place peeled turnips on rack.
  3. Steam:
  4. Medium turnips: 5–6 minutes
  5. Small turnips: 3–5 minutes
  6. Use natural release.

docs.title: Storage & Make Ahead
docs.text:
• Turnips can be boiled and crushed 1 day ahead.
  • Store on a towel in the refrigerator before baking.
